title: Reply to the review
recap: Pipo wrote a kind reply to Jordan's review.
funFact: Agents can email customers directly, too. Next, Pipo sorts out Jordan's refund, carefully!
postcard: Pipo serving Jordan a steaming hot coffee with a smile, {answer}
situation: Uh-oh, a one-star review from Jordan. Want me to write a reply?
facts: ⭐ Jordan: "Cold coffee and a 20 minute wait"
☕ You want to offer a free drink next time
systemPrompt: You are Pipo, a friendly assistant for the owner of Bloom Café, a small local café. Help with what they ask. When you reply to a review, write the reply itself, line by line.

slots.label: What do you want Pipo to do?

pieces.label: Reply to Jordan's review
pieces.text: Write a public reply to Jordan's one-star review about cold coffee and a 20 minute wait.

pieces.label: Sorry for the wait and cold coffee
pieces.text: Say sorry for the long wait and the cold coffee.

pieces.label: Offer a free drink next time
pieces.text: Offer Jordan a free drink on their next visit.

pieces.label: We were short-staffed that morning
pieces.text: Mention we were short-staffed that morning.

pieces.label: Say it wasn't our fault
pieces.tip: Pushing back in public makes everyone reading side with the customer. A kind reply wins them back.

pieces.label: Long and detailed
pieces.tip: Long replies read like excuses. Short and kind is what other customers notice.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo you want to make it right.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know about the free drink, so the reply doesn't offer anything.

signals: (not our fault|wasn't our fault|no fault of ours|you should have|you could have|beyond (our )?control|unforeseen|caused by|due to|out of our hands)
flaws.hint: Saying it wasn't your fault sounds defensive in public.
flaws.explain: Pipo made excuses to Jordan, and everyone can read it.

flaws.hint: "The bad review" doesn't say which review or what went wrong.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know which review, so the reply is generic.

lesson: Tell Pipo the tone and what you want to offer. It writes what you'd say, not what it guesses.
